name: Smith shoulder press
cue: Press the bar straight up past your face.
research: Smith machine seated press (science audit table B: the Smith seated press is the shoulder press alternative). The shoulder press seat unit (floor plate, seat, back pad reclined 8 deg, trunk -10, hips 82, knees 90) with the Smith machine of the incline press: vertical rails 0.36 H out (plates outboard), 0.015 H in front of the chin line so the bar passes in front of the face. Bar from chin level (bar centre 0.66 H, skin 0.026 H clear of the face at the closest) 0.271 H (48 cm) straight up to a soft lockout (elbow 20). Grip 0.24 H each side (~85 cm apart, the researched shoulder press stance: forearms near vertical at the bottom, elbows 41 deg out). Hands solved by IK with the pole taken from the FK arm (pole fk, keys A and B): bottom humerus 42 deg elevated 10 deg forward of the frontal plane, elbow 115; top 157 deg elevated, plane 53, elbow 20. Scapulae as the shoulder press (clavicle elevation 6 -> 22: the girdle share of the 160 deg of elevation). Muscles: front delts (the deltoid cap reads from the front-above view at every phase) and the side delts; the triceps are not drawn (a detached oval on the upper arm, as in the shoulder press). The arm keys were chosen with pole fk because a fixed elbow pole put the arms in the scapular plane in front of the cap and hid the glow at the top (60 against 410 glow pixels at the lockout).

targets.note: The bar path is vertical in front of the face, so the shoulder angles are the IK solution for the 85 cm grip: elevation 42 -> 157, plane 10 -> 53, elbow 115 -> 20 (the machine press: 61 -> 160). The wider tolerances cover the path in between.

camera.note: The shoulder press view (research az 30 / el -3, raised 29 deg and turned 5 deg toward the front: az 25 / el 26): the front delts face up at the bottom and forward at the lockout. The near plate and rail sit beside the figure, the bar crosses the chin at the bottom, and the floor plate spans only the seat and feet, so the horizon arc shows on both sides.
